unextracted: a macro; the extractor records declarations, not macros
why:
`RCLCPP_ERROR_THROTTLE(logger, clock, period, ...)` -- ADOPTED (GitHub #4010, issue 2636). It was REFUSE-LOUD: upstream measures the window on the `clock` argument and C's throttle read `nros_log`'s own clock, so forwarding would have dropped `clock` and compiled and differed. The macro now reads `clock.now()` and passes the reading to `rclc_log_throttle_admit_at`, the C throttle's rule (`nros_log::throttle_decide`) on a caller-supplied reading, so every valid clock is honoured on its own reading: steady, system, and ROS time on system time or driven by `/clock`.

SITE: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp`, `NROS_RCLCPP_LOG_THROTTLE_` and `rclcpp::detail::throttle_admit`. Per-site state is function-local statics -- no heap, no table, no lock -- so it holds on a freestanding target. Test: `log_conditional_runtime` (`just check cpp`, built with and without `NROS_CPP_STD`).

DIVERGENCE, at runtime: an INVALID clock (`RCL_CLOCK_UNINITIALIZED`, whose `now()` reads zero) cannot be read. Upstream then admits every record; this measures the site on the platform's monotonic clock (`rclc_log_throttle_admit`) and says `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_THROTTLE_CLOCK_RUNTIME` at WARN once, because on an embedded target a throttled site is usually a hot loop and letting it through floods the console and the transport. A clock's type is a constructor argument, not part of its C++ type, so this cannot be a compile error.

DIVERGENCE, from the shared rule (per-site storage with no allocator, one rule for C, C++ and Rust): the first record at a site always logs, where upstream's first comparison `now >= 0 + duration` drops it while a simulated clock reads below the window; and a clock that jumps backwards admits, where upstream waits for it to catch up. The siblings `_ONCE`, `_SKIPFIRST` and `_SKIPFIRST_THROTTLE` are adopted in the same header and carry no row: the extractor emits no macros.
